content:
Ok, this is very different from the SPGT formalization and I'm not sure it will be exciting to anyone but me, but I just tried a Trellis run using only GPT-5.6 luna in all roles (the lightweight/smaller model that is 20x cheaper). It completed in a few days, roughly the same amount of time as the original runs I did on this with frontier models (then gpt 5.5).

The paper is Bradač's recent paper on offdiagonal Ramsey numbers. I previously had Trellis formalize this (with frontier models).

This is a short paper but "real math" that made a real breakthrough (I would bet that it was a problem that had been given to the internal models unsuccessfully before Bradač posted it this year). the lean formalization is 11k lines. The paper is here:
https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.28793

I'm running on subscription as usual but at API rates this formalization would have only been around $25. That is 100x less than the API cost of the original frontier-model run, which would have been a few thousand dollars (even though it was just a few days on one subscription). I think a crude estimate is that it probably used 25x less electricity. In particular, Trellis runs like this could continually be produced by a 20$ / month chatgpt subscription with budget to spare.

Formalization is here:
https://github.com/wpegden/offdiagonal-luna

Oh and I should say, since it's the question I would have:

This run had basic defense against web access, the agent logs were scanned afterwards to make sure they didn't browse the web to find Trellis' previous formalization, and the formalizations aren't the same; it really is an independent formalization from the earlier one.
Wow, this is very interesting. I was not expecting to see "end-to-end" formalization at that scale from Luna, so this is really good to know.

Yes I did a comparsion with a generic "agent harness" not developed specifically for a math-formalization pipeline (harmonize flame-chase) and using luna in all roles there was not successful on the same paper (when I stopped it it had gone through around 5x the token-cost and written 5x the LOC as the trellis run but not gotten anywhere close to finishing). So I see this as evidence that it is really possible to extend the capabilities of the agents with a process designed specifically for formalization.

I suspect this means I could be doing Trellis formalizations with open-weight models but ironically, compared with doing things at subscription prices, the frontier open-weights models are too expensive at current hosted prices!
